speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to help me pinpoint the cause, could you please describe exactly when these symptoms started and if they were triggered by any specific event or injury?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; given your background as a bodybuilder with a history of anabolic steroid use, alcohol consumption, and diabetes, combined with significant weight loss, have you noticed any specific weakness in your shoulder or neck muscles, or any neck pain preceding the arm symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: The burning and aching pain you describe, combined with your diabetes and steroid use, raises concern for cervical radiculopathy or a parsonage-turner syndrome variant, but the rapid progression and weight loss are alarming. Have you noticed any difficulty with your grip strength, numbness in specific fingers, or any muscle wasting in your right forearm?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of progressive arm weakness, sensory loss, weight loss, diabetes, and heavy anabolic steroid use is highly concerning for a malignancy, such as a paraspinal tumor compressing the nerve root. Have you noticed any changes in bowel or bladder control, or any numbness in the groin area? REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical Spine.
